candidates.hook: Rupert leans in with venomous malice and says, 'And no one will question what happened to the woman who tried to stop us.'
candidates.cliffhanger: Catherine adds, 'Especially to the Ashcrofts,' implying a specific target for the terror, just before the scene cuts to the invitation being delivered.
candidates.why: It establishes the villains' cold calculation and the dual threat of a wedding and an execution, creating immediate high stakes.
candidates.context_needed: The viewer doesn't know who 'the woman' is or who the Ashcrofts are, but the tone clearly signals a conspiracy against a specific victim.

candidates.hook: A close-up of a bruised, shackled hand trembling inches from a dirty bowl of murky liquid, then pulling away in defiance.
candidates.cliffhanger: Juliana grips the iron ring and declares, 'They cannot take who I am!' leaving the viewer to wonder if her defiance will save her or hasten her death.
candidates.why: The visual of starvation and chains is visceral and instantly sympathetic, while the defiant speech provides a strong emotional hook for the hero.
candidates.context_needed: The viewer doesn't know Juliana's name or why she is there, but the visual language of 'wronged heroine in prison' is universally understood.

candidates.hook: Lady Clarissa unfolds a second page of the invitation and says, 'And after the ceremony...' with intrigue.
candidates.cliffhanger: Clarissa states, 'Not just an execution. A warning,' leaving the specific nature of the warning and the target ambiguous.
candidates.why: It reveals the shocking detail that the wedding invitation includes an execution clause, turning a social event into a public spectacle of violence.
candidates.context_needed: The viewer needs to infer that the 'condemned' is the same woman the villains are targeting, which is implied by the tone.

moments.desc: Rupert and Catherine plot the execution of the woman who tried to stop them, stating it will be a 'feast for our guests' after the wedding.
Juliana, starving and shackled, whispers that they think hunger will make her surrender, then snaps open her eyes and gasps, 'I will not!'
The nobleman reads the invitation and realizes in awe, 'The sentencing of the condemned,' revealing the execution clause attached to the wedding invite.
Lady Clarissa drinks wine and proclaims, 'Let them see what happens when a woman forgets her place,' ending on a chilling threat.
